prompts.question: Error Analysis Anna solved the equation (x^2+8x-20=0) by factoring. She wrote ((x-10)(x+2)=0) and expected the (x)-intercepts of the function (y=x^2+8x-20) to be at -10 and 2. Was she right?
prompts.answer: No; the factored form of the equation is ((x+10)(x-2)=0). Although the (x)-intercepts are correct, Anna incorrectly applied the Zero Product Property. If she had factored the equation correctly, it is unlikely that she would have found the correct (x)-intercepts.

prompts.question: How can a function be both positive and negative? Explain algebraically and graphically.
prompts.answer: A function can be positive for some values and negative for others. Algebraically: A function is positive when an (x)-value gives a positive (y)-value and negative when an (x)-value gives a negative (y)-value. Graphically: When the graph is above the (x)-axis, it is positive, and when it is below the (x)-axis, it is negative.
